answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by binding each identity to a sustained sequential-proof stream that a verifier measures at a fixed full rate per physical core. An attacker trying to harbor ten accounts on one machine must split that core's compute, so every stream falls below the accepted rate and earns nothing; total reward stays capped by cores, not accounts. The proof acts as a pigment marking real, non-shareable work, and the verifier's rate check is the reef blocking cheap clones. Cost is linear in cores, so it deters low-budget attackers but not a funder renting many cores.
